lesson_title: Brown, Blue, Green and Yellow: The Wires That Keep You Alive
hook_text: One wire in your kettle's cable does nothing at all, until the day it saves your life.
clip_script: Cut open an appliance cable and you find three wires. Brown is live: it carries the electricity in at 230 volts. Blue is neutral: it carries the current back to complete the loop. And green and yellow is earth, the safety wire, which normally does nothing at all. Here is its moment. Inside a metal kettle, the insulation cracks and the live wire touches the metal body. Without an earth wire, the kettle looks normal, but it is now at 230 volts, waiting for someone to touch it. With an earth wire, a huge current rushes down that easy path to the ground, the breaker trips, the earth leakage unit switches off, and the danger is gone before anyone reaches for the handle. That is why the earth pin on a plug is the longest: in first, out last. And why switches always go in the brown live wire.
visual_style: A cable sliced to reveal three coloured wires; a cutaway kettle with a spark where insulation fails; animated current racing down the earth wire to a ground rod; a plug with the long earth pin highlighted.
pacing: Mysterious hook, quick colour roll call, a tense fault scenario, a confident safety finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and check the plugs in your home for damage.
